heading: Winter in the Okanagan, without the downhill
title: Winter Beyond the Ski Hills | Okanagan Roam
description: Tube parks, fat bikes, lit forest trails, snowshoe dinners, ice fishing and winter birding: Okanagan winter fun that doesn't need a lift ticket.
intro: Not everyone in the group wants to ski all day, and plenty of people don't ski at all. The Okanagan's mountain villages and valley towns have a whole second winter going on: tube parks that run into the evening, trails built for fat bikes, lit forest walks and snowshoe dinners, plus quiet lakeshore spots where the winter birds gather.

{page:/guides/okanagan-skating|Skating rinks} and {page:/guides/okanagan-nordic-snowshoe|cross-country and snowshoe trails} have their own guides, and so do {page:/guides/okanagan-sleigh-rides-dog-sledding|sleigh rides, dog sledding and snowmobile tours}, so this one sticks to everything else. Mountain conditions change fast, so check each operator's hours before you drive up.

items.name: Big White Tube Park (Happy Valley)
items.text: Five specially groomed lanes and a tube lift, with no skill or equipment needed. Tickets are sold for timed two-hour windows and only a limited number go on sale, so book online ahead.

items.name: Tube Town – SilverStar Tube Park
items.text: Truck-sized tubes, several lanes and a tube lift beside Brewer's Pond, included in the resort's My1Pass. Next door, a fenced mini-snowmobile track lets children aged six to twelve (under 100 lb) drive supervised laps.

items.name: Tim Hortons Tube Park – Apex
items.text: At the base area beside the beginner slopes, running on weekends and holidays through the season. On Friday and Saturday nights it runs under the lights from 4 to 9 pm, with tickets sold in two-hour blocks.

items.name: Baldy Mountain Resort
items.text: The Magic Carpet stays open until 7 pm on Friday and Saturday nights for tubing and beginner skiing under the lights. You can also borrow discs at the ticket office for winter disc golf beside the Sugarlump Chair.

items.name: SilverStar Fat Bike Trails
items.text: 15 kilometres of packed, signed single- and double-track, with fat bike rentals in the village. Stay off the trails when the temperature climbs above zero.

items.name: Big White Winter eBike Tours
items.text: One-hour guided fat-tire e-bike rides on snowy backcountry trails, from a 9am intro ride to a 3pm intermediate outing. Groups max 4, riders 15+.

items.name: Twinkling Trail – Big White
items.text: An illuminated walking path through the snowy forest of the Happy Valley Adventure Park, open to all ages and lit from dusk. No equipment and no skill are needed, and leashed dogs are welcome.

items.name: Ravenwood Snowshoe Dinner Tours – SilverStar
items.text: A guided snowshoe through the darkening forest to Ravenwood Cabin, where dinner is waiting. Dates and pricing for the coming winter are announced by the resort and booked through Guest Services.

sections.heading: Frozen lakes and quiet winter outings

items.name: Rodney's REEL Outdoors – Ice Fishing Charters
items.text: Full-day ice-fishing charters to a trout lake, with gear, an ice hut, a fire on shore and a hot lunch supplied. A BC freshwater fishing licence is required and not included.

items.name: Echo Lake Provincial Park
items.text: A forested mountain lake reached by about 20 km of gravel road, popular for fishing for rainbow trout, lake trout and kokanee in both summer and winter.

items.name: Maude-Roxby Wetland (Bird Sanctuary)
items.text: A raised boardwalk leads to a viewing platform over the lake. Winter brings rafts of gulls and waterfowl, with tundra and trumpeter swans possible; no dogs are allowed.

items.name: Rotary Marsh Park
items.text: A restored wetland at the north end of Waterfront Park, where loons, grebes, hooded mergansers and diving ducks gather off the point in winter. It is free and open year-round, and no dogs are allowed.

items.name: Osoyoos Curling Club
items.text: A friendly community club with leagues, social draws and free Learn to Curl clinics for first-timers.
